subject: SIG evidence: proposed sampling plan for retention & deletion
messages:

Cc: Aurelia Security Team <security@aureliatherapeutics.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG evidence request — retention & deletion sampling

Hi Olga,

Thanks for taking this. As part of our SIG and downstream legal review we need granular evidence showing how Redwood handles data retention, deletion, and related audit logs for our tenant. High-level answers are fine for the questionnaire, but we also need an evidence package we can attach to the SIG submission. Specifically: 

- A short plan describing how you will provide a sampling of deleted records (redacted) and associated audit-log entries.
- One or two example audit-log snapshots showing deletion events and correlating request IDs.
- The exact policy text that governs log TTLs and any customer-specific retention overrides.
- An attestation from Redwood that the samples represent production behaviour (signed).

We attached the full SIG questionnaire (attached as SIG-questionnaire-2026.xlsx). Can you confirm what format is acceptable for the samples (CSV/JSON) and whether redaction is permissible for PII? Also let us know an estimated delivery window — our deadline to submit the completed evidence package is 2026-10-01.

Appreciate it — Jenna
Jenna Hsu
Security Program Manager
Aurelia Therapeutics

Attachment: SIG-questionnaire-2026.xlsx (spreadsheet, 1 sheet)

Hi Jenna — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Rishi (security) and Laura (compliance) to confirm the technical approach + delivery.

Short answer: we can provide a scoped, redacted sample plus an attestation. Proposed deliverables:

1) A one-page retention snapshot (policy excerpt + TTL table)
2) A redacted sample of deleted items (N=50 by default) in JSONL, with request IDs masked but event timestamps preserved
3) Audit-log snapshots that show the deletion events correlated to request IDs (redactions applied where necessary)
4) A signed attestation (we can provide a DocuSign link)

Questions for Aurelia:
- Is CSV acceptable or do you prefer JSONL? We typically provide JSONL for logs.
- For redaction: we'll redact email addresses and any direct PII values; are hashed identifiers acceptable for your auditors?

Rishi/Laura — can you confirm the sampling window we should use (we propose last 30 days for request-level deletions, and a second sample for the 90-day system-level retention events)? Also flag any customer-specific exceptions (Aurelia might have asked for an extended retention in your legal notes).

Timeline: if we confirm scope today we can deliver the samples and attestation within 7 business days. If you need a tighter window we can prioritize.

Thanks,

Hi all — quick technical note on what we can include and how we handle retention by default. Attaching a short plan (redwood-retention-sampling-plan.pdf) and an anonymized audit snapshot (audit-log-snapshot-20260914.jsonl).

Key points:
- Default retention: request-level logs (API request/response metadata) are retained 30 days by default. System-level telemetry that supports reliability/monitoring is retained 90 days.
- KV caches and model inference ephemeral state are not persisted beyond active session windows (typically <48 hours) and are not included in audits.
- Deletion flow: when a tenant requests deletion, we mark the tenant resource for deletion, enqueue a job that performs data purging, and emit deletion events to the audit stream. Those events include request_id, timestamp, actor_id, and resource_type. In samples we'll redact actor_id/email.
- For customer-specific exceptions (Aurelia asked about a longer preservation window) — we require an approved Exception Request (security review + product sign-off). If approved, we record the exception id and include it in the evidence.

Sampling approach I recommend:
- Sample A: last 30 days of deletion events (N=50) — include request_id (hashed), timestamp, resource_type, and a minimal context field.
- Sample B: a single system-level TTL snapshot that shows the retention policy table and any configured overrides for the customer.

I've attached the two files for illustration. The audit-log snapshot is redacted and generated from a synthetic extraction to avoid sharing PII. If Aurelia wants salted hashes instead of full redaction, tell us which hashing scheme to use and we'll apply it.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-retention-sampling-plan.pdf, audit-log-snapshot-20260914.jsonl

From: Jenna Hsu <jenna.hsu@aureliatherapeutics.com>

Thanks Rishi — this looks good and answers most of our questions. A couple of follow-ups: 

- JSONL is preferred for the samples (we'll ingest to our evidence repo).
- Hashed identifiers are acceptable; please use SHA-256 and include a short description of the salt usage (or state if no salt is used).
- For the attestation: we need a named signatory and company letterhead. Can you provide the attestation as a DocuSign envelope?

If you can deliver the two samples (A and B) plus the attestation within 10 business days that meets our internal deadline. After we ingest the evidence we may have one short clarifying question, but this should be sufficient for the SIG review.

One operational ask — please include the exception id if Aurelia has previously requested a longer retention window (we'll cross-check against our legal notes).

Appreciate the quick turn.

—Jenna
